tasks.short: Select wastewater equipment that meets government standards.

steps.what: Extract government standards that the equipment must meet.

loop.input: The government standard and the duty statement
loop.output: Limit table: parameter, unit, limit and clause reference
loop.check: Engineer checks each limit against the clause
loop.stop: One pass; a limit without a clause stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Standards mix tables and numbered clauses a fixed map misses

steps.what: Select candidate equipment from the supplier data sheets.

loop.input: Supplier data sheets and the limit table
loop.output: Candidate list with stated duty and the matched limit
loop.check: Engineer confirms each match against the sheet
loop.stop: One pass; an unmatched duty is marked open
loop.why_not_simpler: Sheet layouts differ by supplier, so one template does not cover them

steps.what: Supplier engineer confirms the wastewater duty curve.
Check each curve against the compliance limits.
Judge which equipment complies and fits the process.
Send the equipment selection for government review.

loop.input: Selection judgement and the compliance sheet
loop.output: Selection pack naming the equipment, the limit and the clause
loop.check: Engineer checks every limit before send
loop.stop: One draft; a limit not on the sheet is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The pack must cite the clause, which a blank letter does not

tasks.design: Government limits are read into a table in {DOCS}, and supplier curves are checked against that table in {SPREADSHEET}. The engineer still judges which equipment fits the process. The pack goes to the agency only after that judgement is checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards and supplier sheets were separate files, so every limit was retyped into the comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Clause fields and a curve table can be compared before the judgement. The fit to the process stays.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a unit meets the number but will not run on this wastewater.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer knows which clause is absolute and which duty the supplier has overstated.

ambition.what: Drop a candidate that misses a numeric government limit before the supplier meeting, instead of discovering it in the pack.

tasks.altitude: Selection meetings stay. The engineer can refuse to send a pack that still has a blank clause.

reach.task: Rate a pump or blower against a stated duty
reach.learn: Which curve points the compliance check must not smooth over

evidence.claim: A numeric limit can be checked in code; the engineer still judges a non-standard case.
The signing engineer stays responsible for what is issued.
Safety components in water supply are treated as high-risk under the EU AI Act.

assumptions: Focal role is the water engineer. Boundary: from a duty statement and a government standard to the selection sent for review. Plant layout is out of scope.
Test {SPREADSHEET} formulas and {DOCS} properties before custom code.

Structured fields are parameter, unit, limit, clause, equipment name and stated duty. The agency text and the supplier sheet produce them. Fallback: the engineer types a blank limit and the check waits.
Passing the numeric check is not the selection.
unknowns: Which standards apply as numbers and which are narrative.
Whether the agency accepts a pack from the engineer or only from the client.
research_questions: Which equipment types have no stable numeric limit in the standard the client cites?

already_counted.description: Judging units that pass the number but may not run
Checking the selection pack before send

incremental.description: Update limit tables when a cited standard is reissued

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A repeat duty with a numeric standard saves the extract and the curve check. Narrative clauses, the process fit and the agency pack stay. The low case is a standard that will not split into limits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design pumping stations, force mains and collection sewers.

steps.what: Survey technician measures invert levels for the sewers.
Set the pumping design flow and the receiving level.
Calculate force mains head loss and diameter.
Place pumping stations and the wet well on the plan.
Check collection sewer slopes against the pumping head.
Walk the client through the pumping station layout.
Issue the pumping systems design for review.

loop.input: Force main sheet, slope sheet and station layout list
loop.output: Pumping issue naming diameters, heads and the layout version
loop.check: Engineer checks every head and diameter against the sheets
loop.stop: One draft; a figure not on a sheet is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The issue must match this calculation, not a previous main

tasks.design: Invert levels come from the survey. Force-main head loss and sewer slopes are calculated in {SPREADSHEET} from the design flow the engineer sets. The station layout and the client walk stay. The issue goes out only after the engineer checks heads and diameters.
tasks.previous_blocker: Levels, slopes and heads were copied between a survey file and a fresh workbook for every main.
tasks.enabler_now: Once flow and inverts are fields, head loss and slope are a formula. Siting the station stays a drawing.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a wet-well level when the survey and the receiving sewer disagree.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer sees a station site that the head-loss number treats as flat ground.
tasks.altitude: Pumping design stays on the week. The engineer can hold an issue when an invert or a head is blank.

reach.task: Measure invert and cover along a sewer route
reach.learn: Which shots are offset or blocked and cannot be used as a design level

evidence.claim: A numeric limit can be checked in code; the engineer still judges a non-standard case.
The signing engineer stays responsible for what is issued.
Site layout from levels and constraints is existing design work, not a text summary.

assumptions: Focal role is the water engineer. Boundary: from invert survey and design flow to the issued pumping design. Treatment-plant process design is out of scope.
Test native {SPREADSHEET} formulas before custom code.

Structured fields are invert, ground level, design flow, pipe diameter, length, roughness and head. The surveying technician produces levels. Fallback: a missing invert is typed by the engineer and marked unchecked.
Placing the station and walking the client are not calculations.
unknowns: Whether inverts arrive as a coordinate file or a marked plan.
Who owns the receiving sewer level.
research_questions: Which force mains need a surge check the steady formula does not cover?

already_counted.description: Setting flow and receiving level when the survey conflicts

incremental.description: Keep roughness and fitting allowances current for the firm's mains
Survey time for a return visit when a level is blocked

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A straight force main with a complete survey saves the head-loss and slope pass. Station siting, the client walk and surge cases stay. The low case is a route with missing inverts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design potable or non-potable water distribution systems.

steps.what: Gather potable demand and fire flow for distribution.

loop.input: Demand brief and the hydrant standard
loop.output: Demand sheet: node, average flow, peak flow and fire flow
loop.check: Engineer checks each node against the brief
loop.stop: One pass; a node without a flow stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Demands arrive as notes and sketches, not one table

steps.what: Run the distribution model for pressure and head loss.
Judge where distribution pressure or residual would fail.
Check distribution tie-ins on site before issuing.
Issue the water distribution design to the client.

loop.input: Pressure results, judgement and tie-in notes
loop.output: Distribution issue with the case name and the minimum pressure
loop.check: Engineer checks each pressure against the result table
loop.stop: One draft; a pressure not in the table is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The note must name the case that was run, not a generic summary

tasks.design: Node demands are stored on the {PROJECT} record and the distribution model returns pressure and head loss. The engineer judges where residual would fail and still checks tie-ins on site. The client receives the design only after that version is checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Demands were retyped into the model, and the site tie-in was often found after the first issue.
tasks.enabler_now: A demand table can drive the pressure run. Judging a failed node and seeing the tie-in stay.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether a low pressure is a pipe size, a wrong demand, or a closed valve in the field.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer can tell a model failure from a tie-in that the drawing has in the wrong street.

ambition.what: Run the fire-flow case on every distribution design before the drawing, not only when the client asks.

tasks.altitude: Distribution design stays. The engineer can refuse an issue that has no fire-flow case or an unchecked tie-in.

reach.task: Trace an existing main and valve from records
reach.learn: Which valves are normally closed and would void the model

evidence.claim: A numeric limit can be checked in code; the engineer still judges a non-standard case.
The signing engineer stays responsible for what is issued.
Safety components in water supply are treated as high-risk under the EU AI Act.

assumptions: Focal role is the water engineer. Boundary: from demands and pipe records to the issued distribution design. Treatment design is out of scope.
Test the model's native scenario tables before custom code.
Structured fields are node, average flow, peak flow, fire flow, diameter and roughness. The client produces the demand brief. Fallback: the engineer types a blank node and that case is not issued.
The site check of tie-ins is not a model run.
unknowns: Whether fire-flow is a number in the hydrant standard or a local rule.
Whether the model and the drawing share one pipe identity.
research_questions: Which networks are too incomplete to run without a field survey?

already_counted.description: Judging nodes that fail pressure or residual

incremental.description: Keep demand patterns and roughness defaults aligned with the model

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A complete demand table saves the extract and most of the model pass. Failed nodes, the site tie-in and the issue check stay. The low case is a network with unknown valves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study water quality and characterize pollutant sources.

steps.what: Map likely pollutant sources before the quality study.
Collect water samples at the mapped pollutant sources.
Laboratory technician analyses the water quality samples.
Characterize which source fits the sample results.

tasks.design: The sample plan is a marked map, not a generated essay. The engineer still collects the water samples. Lab results return as fields, and the engineer characterizes the source in {SPREADSHEET} before any note is sent. Native result columns are used before custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample points and lab tables lived in different files, and the source story was rewritten for each study.
tasks.enabler_now: Result fields can be lined up with the sample plan. Choosing the point and taking the sample stay.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a true source from a lab blank, a storm spike, or a source the map missed.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer stood at the bank and knows which sample point does not match the map.

ambition.what: Give the plant operator the source note, not only the client who commissioned the study.

tasks.altitude: Sampling days stay. The engineer can withhold a source note that is not tied to a sample identity.

reach.task: Trace an upstream discharge to a structure
reach.learn: Which outfalls on the map are abandoned and should not be sampled

evidence.claim: Lining lab results up with sample points is a table, not a judgement of the source.
A water-quality conclusion that names a polluter can have legal effect, so the engineer signs it.
The signing engineer stays responsible for what is issued.

assumptions: Focal role is the water engineer. Boundary: from the map of possible sources to a signed characterization. Designing treatment is out of scope.
Test the laboratory file's native columns before custom code.

Structured fields are sample identity, location, time, determinant and result. The laboratory produces the results. Fallback: the engineer types a result that arrived on paper and marks it unverified.
Collecting samples is physical work and stays.
unknowns: Whether the lab file uses the same sample identity as the plan.
Which determinants are accredited for this matrix.
research_questions: Which sources can be named only after a second visit?

already_counted.description: Matching results to sources the first screen cannot separate
Choosing sample points the map leaves ambiguous

incremental.description: Maintain determinant names so lab files still match the plan

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A repeat catchment with matching sample identities saves only the lining up of results. Mapping, sampling and the source judgement stay. The low case is a wet-weather study with points the map did not show.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Equipment selection, pumping design, distribution models and sampling days stay. Less time goes to retyping limits, inverts and lab columns.
reach: Mechanical engineers rating a pump curve
skills_to_grow: Writing a government limit as a field with a clause
Refusing a model issue when a node or an invert is blank
Keeping sample identities aligned with the laboratory
role.ambitious_version: The engineer can drop a non-compliant equipment candidate, and can run fire flow, before anyone is asked to a meeting.
